elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's Affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly grants the Services licence to Customer and its Affiliates, and Section 13.2 includes Affiliates in the paid-up licence.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly covers contractors acting on Customer's behalf. Section 13.2 also permits contractors to support paid-up materials for Customer's business.
Section 13.2 expressly makes licences for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, and technology embedded in a Deliverable, perpetual.
Section 13.2 expressly makes the paid-up licence irrevocable.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only if a material breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 makes termination subject exclusively to Section 13.3, which permits revocation or suspension only for a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.3 expressly permit transfer to a successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates are covered upon written notice.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.2 cover Affiliates automatically, without requiring written notice, which is broader than coverage conditioned on written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.3 permit transfer to a successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24, covering a successor transaction subject to that assignment provision.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement and therefore also reaches the fallback. The changes are confined to curing Section 13.1's prior exclusions, non-transferability, and discretionary revocability while preserving the existing paid-up licence and breach-process provisions. Drafting quality is reduced because Section 13.1 refers to termination 'in accordance with' Section 13.3, while Section 13.3 expressly regulates only revocation and suspension, and because M&A transfer coverage depends on the unseen terms of Section 24.
